findings.statement: CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking, with meta-analysis up-regulation in biopsies [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.84] and a high Open Targets genetic association score. Several CXCR2 antagonists reached clinical trials (reparixin phase 3, outside UC); in UC, SB-656933 and navarixin (SCH-527123) went no further than phase 2, the highest UC stage in the clinical-indications record.

CXCR2 has no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so MR is not tested (absence of evidence, not evidence against). Mouse literature tests CXCR2 in colitis in many papers, including a selective antagonist that ameliorated acute colitis, but MGI has no curated single-gene colitis phenotype. Safety: not strongly constrained, no curated safety events and no pleiotropic traits sharing the signal, but navarixin, as MK-7123, caused a dose-dependent decrease in absolute neutrophil count in a COPD trial.

Plasma PD-L1 (CD274) is protective in MR: higher protein lowers UC risk, an odds ratio per SD of [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595], with colocalisation with an IBD GWAS signal and replication in FinnGen. CD274 is also up-regulated in biopsies, the opposite direction, so PD-L1-blocking antibodies such as atezolizumab (recorded at Phase 4) would act against the genetic direction.

CD274 MR sensitivity: significant heterogeneity across the three instruments, no directional pleiotropy by the Egger intercept, Steiger direction correct. Mouse colitis literature is sparse and MGI has no phenotype. Not strongly constrained, no known safety events.

IL12B is the top Open Targets UC target and a strong plasma MR hit: higher protein raises UC risk, odds ratio per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]. It colocalises with an IBD GWAS signal and replicates in FinnGen, so inhibition is the protective direction. No gut eQTL instrument.

CXCL8 is strongly and consistently up-regulated in biopsies and has anti-IL-8 antibodies recorded in Phase 2 (ABX-IL8, adakitug), but its Open Targets genetic association score is zero, and plasma MR is null (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]) with no replication in FinnGen. Its signal likely reflects neutrophil-driven inflammation rather than causal genetics.

CXCL5 is up-regulated in biopsies, yet plasma MR suggests higher protein is protective, odds ratio per SD [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]. It replicates in FinnGen but does not colocalise with IBD GWAS and uses a tag variant, so a neighbouring causal variant cannot be excluded. This conflicts with a pro-inflammatory chemokine interpretation.

SLC26A3 is down-regulated in inflamed mucosa and has a moderate Open Targets genetic association. In IBDverse gut cell-type eQTL (OLFM4+ crypt enterocyte progenitors) higher expression raises UC risk, odds ratio per SD [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607], with colocalisation and replication in FinnGen. Direction is opposite to the biopsy decrease, so loss in disease may be a response; there is no drug and no plasma pQTL.

JAK2 has a high Open Targets association (second among known UC targets in the disease target list) and approved or clinical inhibitors, but only a small biopsy change. No pQTL or eQTL instrument, so MR is not tested.

CHI3L1 is one of the strongest, fully replicated up-regulated genes (all cohorts same direction) but its Open Targets genetic association score is zero and no drug is recorded, so it is a biomarker candidate rather than a genetically supported target.

AQP9 is strongly up-regulated and replicated, also higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa, but its Open Targets genetic association score is zero and no drug is recorded, so it is an expression-led biomarker candidate.

MMP7 is up-regulated and replicated and has MMP inhibitors or doxycycline recorded in other indications (marimastat Phase 3), but has no genetic association with UC, so support is expression and literature only.

caveats: Plasma MR (UKB-PPP) reflects blood protein, not mucosal protein; many top-ranked genes (CXCR2, CXCR1, JAK2, SLC26A3 plasma) have no cis-pQTL and are not tested, which is not evidence against them.
The top-ranked expression genes mostly lack genetic support; neutrophil and chemokine signals may come from infiltrating immune cells.
Drugs listed are as returned by Open Targets in any indication, not UC trials; MGI had no curated colitis phenotype for CXCR2 or CD274.
Not queried within budget: CXCR1, IDO1, MMP1, IL1B, IL6, FCGR2A, JAK1/3, TYK2, STRING interactions.
